P1.display-mode.title: Switch between two and three displayed dimensions

P1.playback.title: Play a dimension forward and backward

P2.clipping-planes.title: Position image planes and clipping planes

P3.tracks.title: Use Tracks layers and division graphs

P4.label-fill-preserve.title: Control connected fill and label preservation

P4.label-tools.title: Paint, erase, fill, pick, and polygon-label

P5.incremental-workflow.title: View, edit, process, and export large data

P5.lazy-open.title: Open native arrays without eager materialization

P7.dynamic-controls.title: Resolve dependent controls in the worker

P8.execution.title: Run scientific workflows on each platform

P8.install.title: Install natively on three operating systems

P8.updates.title: Preserve work through app and package updates

R01.producing-history.title: Two kernels plus manual editing share a base; after save/restart/export, every accepted result resolves its exact producing history, settings and base, including conflict copies.

R02.new-layer-publication.title: Python and a plugin each create new Image/Labels/Points/Shapes/Surface/Vectors/Tracks outputs; accept and reopen valid outputs with exact data/relations. No startup-only binding restriction.

R03.multi-layer-drafts.title: Edit multiple layers, save one, fail another, resolve a conflict and accept the remainder; all drafts remain available and no partial save appears complete.

R04.resource-only-code.title: Compute and publish using exact undisplayed resources with no fake camera/render receipt; stale resource revisions are refused.

R05.empty-install-intake.title: Empty installed app opens ordinary native datasets and creates scientific documents through public controls, without fixture injection or shell setup.

R06.native-composition.title: Native and structured multiple inputs flow through operation → retained output → next operation for manual/agent/researcher/recipe paths; no RGB conversion or source retargeting.

R07.direct-3d.title: Real gestures orbit/pan/zoom and perform valid 3D picking at multiple DPI/viewport sizes; late frames cannot misplace selections or edits.

R08.specialist-widget.title: A custom stateful panel with actual canvas drag events, live multi-layer choices and asynchronous callbacks works through SDK lifecycle/reconnect without duplicate actions.

R09.truthful-closure.title: Missing child/UI path, stale artifact, null criterion, required skip, failed simulation or unauthenticated admission evidence prevents completion/readiness.

W.partial-batches.title: Retain partial batch and recipe outcomes

children.oracle: Three ways: what the Studio shows and the actual review worker's native state (one shared napari snapshot, read through the Python panel) must equal the same steps in a plain pinned napari Viewer process on the prepared runtime's own Python (tests/scientific_napari_reference.py), and the values the fixture's definition gives independently (tests/scientific_dims_fixture.py). Executed by tests/test_scientific_dims_browser.py::test_axis_labels_and_units_are_napari_s_and_shown_on_every_axis, and by the harness self-check test_the_comparison_catches_a_worker_whose_napari_behaviour_was_broken, which breaks napari inside the worker and needs the same comparisons to fail.
children.procedure: Isolated profile: a new Chromium profile (HOOKE_BROWSER) on a private orchestrator with an empty home, no camera and the Studio rebuilt from the checkout (its build identity must equal the backend). The asymmetric TCZYX uint16 fixture (5x3x7x11x13, each voxel holding its flat index) is a saved scene document of the prepared review integration (NAPARI_NATIVE_HOST_PREPARATION). It is opened from Project Data (Open result, then Open session) and calibrated in the session's Python panel: scale 2.5/1/0.75/0.4/0.3, translate 10/0/-3/5/7, axis labels t/c/z/y/x, units second/pixel/micrometer.  Then: In the Python panel set viewer.dims.axis_labels, then dims.set_axis_label(2, ...), viewer.dims.units, viewer.layers.units, the layer's units, and the layer's labels and units back; press Check current view after each and read every axis row, coordinate line and the playback axis choices.

Asymmetric 5D native arrays (unequal T/C/Z/Y/X, anisotropic spacing, channel identity, index-encoded values, integer and float types, nonzero slices, rotation/translation/affine) are used.

"Reorder and select displayed axes" is compared with pinned napari on frozen reference source, data, hardware, renderer and cache conditions, with numeric/render tolerances and a no-worse rule frozen before the final run; every attempt is kept.

Each applicable injected failure during "Reorder and select displayed axes" (malformed input, dependency conflict, denied access, missing artifact, low disk, interrupted write, hang/crash, cancel, reconnect, stale revision, failed upgrade, revoked authorization, incomplete cleanup) is reported, leaves unrelated jobs, acquisition, saved work and generations intact, terminates owned workers and grants, and a corrected retry succeeds; the first failure evidence is kept.
"Reorder and select displayed axes" begins through ordinary Open, Project Data, layer controls, Tools or a declared panel of the installed app, with no private fixture injection.

"Reorder and select displayed axes" is operated with representative mouse/trackpad and keyboard paths; focus, labels and help, disabled reasons, shortcut conflicts and the current selection are correct.
Switching Tab or Project, closing and reopening the panel or window and restarting the app during "Reorder and select displayed axes" keep background work on its original input and destination.

After "Reorder and select displayed axes", the exact saved scientific values, features, relations and provenance are inspected, then exported and reimported (or reopened across OSes where applicable).
"Reorder and select displayed axes" repeats at the declared viewport sizes and device-pixel scales, resizing during interaction, with no clipping and an exact screen-to-data mapping.
"Reorder and select displayed axes" shows preview versus accepted state, busy, error and cancel states, and stale/conflict recovery, preserving drafts and other unsaved layers.

It is opened from Project Data (Open result, then Open session) and calibrated in the session's Python panel: scale 2.5/1/0.75/0.4/0.3, translate 10/0/-3/5/7, axis labels t/c/z/y/x, units second/pixel/micrometer.  Then: Play t from 1..3 at 10 per second: Once forward from 1 and from 3, Once backward from 3; Loop and Back and forth forward from 1 and Loop backward from 3, pressing Stop after 7, 7 and 5 slices. At 2 per second: Loop from 1 (Stop after 3), Once 1..4 from 1 and from 4. Then enter First 3, Last 1 and press Play.

children.oracle: Three ways: the slices the Studio requested, each frame the worker returned for it and whether its pixels were fetched to draw, against (a) napari's own QtDims.play/AnimationThread driven in a plain pinned napari Viewer process on the prepared runtime's Python (its frames in order and the time of the first), and (b) sequences written out independently from AnimationThread's rules. Executed by tests/test_scientific_dims_browser.py::test_playback_plays_each_loop_mode_both_directions_stops_and_refuses_invalid_ranges, and by the harness self-check test_the_comparison_catches_a_worker_whose_napari_behaviour_was_broken, which breaks napari inside the worker and needs the same comparisons to fail.

"Inspect a finite slab" is compared with pinned napari on frozen reference source, data, hardware, renderer and cache conditions, with numeric/render tolerances and a no-worse rule frozen before the final run; every attempt is kept.

Each applicable injected failure during "Inspect a finite slab" (malformed input, dependency conflict, denied access, missing artifact, low disk, interrupted write, hang/crash, cancel, reconnect, stale revision, failed upgrade, revoked authorization, incomplete cleanup) is reported, leaves unrelated jobs, acquisition, saved work and generations intact, terminates owned workers and grants, and a corrected retry succeeds; the first failure evidence is kept.
"Inspect a finite slab" begins through ordinary Open, Project Data, layer controls, Tools or a declared panel of the installed app, with no private fixture injection.
"Inspect a finite slab" is operated with representative mouse/trackpad and keyboard paths; focus, labels and help, disabled reasons, shortcut conflicts and the current selection are correct.
Switching Tab or Project, closing and reopening the panel or window and restarting the app during "Inspect a finite slab" keep background work on its original input and destination.
After "Inspect a finite slab", the exact saved scientific values, features, relations and provenance are inspected, then exported and reimported (or reopened across OSes where applicable).
"Inspect a finite slab" repeats at the declared viewport sizes and device-pixel scales, resizing during interaction, with no clipping and an exact screen-to-data mapping.
"Inspect a finite slab" shows preview versus accepted state, busy, error and cancel states, and stale/conflict recovery, preserving drafts and other unsaved layers.

children.oracle: The pinned reference. After each recipe, the session's napari state equals the state plain pinned napari reaches by applying the requirement's own setter with the same values: each layer's public state, its data by digest, and the camera. Examples are rendering, attenuation, iso_threshold, interpolation3d, depiction, plane, experimental_clipping_planes, shading, the wireframe and normals parts, and camera.update. The reference rebuilt from the session's layer-data tuples first equals the session. The control also shows the value the worker reports back, and the rendered preview's pixels change. For the isosurface threshold, a higher threshold lights fewer pixels; the Shading control offers exactly none, flat and smooth, and each renders the mesh differently. No matched native screenshot is claimed.
children.procedure: A private Hooke (its own home, assets and empty keys; no camera, keychain or phone; free ports) serves the production Studio build. A fresh browser profile opens a retained 3D volume, and another a retained surface mesh (captured from the same worker as an ordinary output), from Project Data (Data, Open result, Open session, Refresh preview) in the prepared confined napari review bundle (`NAPARI_NATIVE_HOST_PREPARATION`). It operates the ordinary View controls and presses Apply view changes (services/tests/scientific_browser_p2.mjs, `HOOKE_BROWSER`). Before each Apply it records the control's upstream equivalent, and after each recipe it reads the session's napari state through Studio's own Python console. A plain pinned-napari process (`NAPARI_REFERENCE_PYTHON -I`, services/tests/scientific_reference_replay.py) rebuilds the same layers from their layer-data tuples and replays the equivalents. Run by tests/test_scientific_browser_p2.py in `make scientific-acceptance`.

detail.title: Press and hold for move camera mode

children.requirement: Offer the action "Press and hold for move camera mode" (`hold_for_pan_zoom`) with its pinned-upstream effect.

"Control a three-dimensional camera" is compared with pinned napari on frozen reference source, data, hardware, renderer and cache conditions, with numeric/render tolerances and a no-worse rule frozen before the final run; every attempt is kept.

Each applicable injected failure during "Control a three-dimensional camera" (malformed input, dependency conflict, denied access, missing artifact, low disk, interrupted write, hang/crash, cancel, reconnect, stale revision, failed upgrade, revoked authorization, incomplete cleanup) is reported, leaves unrelated jobs, acquisition, saved work and generations intact, terminates owned workers and grants, and a corrected retry succeeds; the first failure evidence is kept.
"Control a three-dimensional camera" begins through ordinary Open, Project Data, layer controls, Tools or a declared panel of the installed app, with no private fixture injection.

"Control a three-dimensional camera" is operated with representative mouse/trackpad and keyboard paths; focus, labels and help, disabled reasons, shortcut conflicts and the current selection are correct.
Switching Tab or Project, closing and reopening the panel or window and restarting the app during "Control a three-dimensional camera" keep background work on its original input and destination.

children.oracle: The pinned reference. After each recipe, the session's napari state equals the state plain pinned napari reaches by applying the requirement's own setter with the same values: each layer's public state, its data by digest, and the camera. Examples are rendering, attenuation, iso_threshold, interpolation3d, depiction, plane, experimental_clipping_planes, shading, the wireframe and normals parts, and camera.update. The reference rebuilt from the session's layer-data tuples first equals the session. The control also shows the value the worker reports back, and the rendered preview's pixels change. For the isosurface threshold, a higher threshold lights fewer pixels; the Shading control offers exactly none, flat and smooth, and each renders the mesh differently. No matched native screenshot is claimed.
children.procedure: A private Hooke (its own home, assets and empty keys; no camera, keychain or phone; free ports) serves the production Studio build. A fresh browser profile opens a retained 3D volume, and another a retained surface mesh (captured from the same worker as an ordinary output), from Project Data (Data, Open result, Open session, Refresh preview) in the prepared confined napari review bundle (`NAPARI_NATIVE_HOST_PREPARATION`). It operates the ordinary View controls and presses Apply view changes (services/tests/scientific_browser_p2.mjs, `HOOKE_BROWSER`). Before each Apply it records the control's upstream equivalent, and after each recipe it reads the session's napari state through Studio's own Python console. A plain pinned-napari process (`NAPARI_REFERENCE_PYTHON -I`, services/tests/scientific_reference_replay.py) rebuilds the same layers from their layer-data tuples and replays the equivalents. Run by tests/test_scientific_browser_p2.py in `make scientific-acceptance`.

It operates the ordinary View controls and presses Apply view changes (services/tests/scientific_browser_p2.mjs, `HOOKE_BROWSER`). Before each Apply it records the control's upstream equivalent, and after each recipe it reads the session's napari state through Studio's own Python console. A plain pinned-napari process (`NAPARI_REFERENCE_PYTHON -I`, services/tests/scientific_reference_replay.py) rebuilds the same layers from their layer-data tuples and replays the equivalents. Run by tests/test_scientific_browser_p2.py in `make scientific-acceptance`.
children.requirement: Read and change `SurfaceNormals.vertex` with its pinned-upstream meaning, through an ordinary Hooke control or its API equivalent.

children.criteria: Every mapped parametrized case executes in the production-path browser and passes with zero skips; states are equal after normalization (floats to 12 significant digits, frozen before the first comparison run).
children.hooke_equivalent: The Studio's View controls of a scientific session (Data, Open result, Open session; the View tab; Apply view changes), over the confined napari review worker.
children.oracle: The pinned reference. After each recipe, the session's napari state equals the state plain pinned napari reaches by applying the requirement's own setter with the same values: each layer's public state, its data by digest, and the camera. Examples are rendering, attenuation, iso_threshold, interpolation3d, depiction, plane, experimental_clipping_planes, shading, the wireframe and normals parts, and camera.update. The reference rebuilt from the session's layer-data tuples first equals the session. The control also shows the value the worker reports back, and the rendered preview's pixels change. For the isosurface threshold, a higher threshold lights fewer pixels; the Shading control offers exactly none, flat and smooth, and each renders the mesh differently. No matched native screenshot is claimed.

Asymmetric 5D native arrays (unequal T/C/Z/Y/X, anisotropic spacing, channel identity, index-encoded values, integer and float types, nonzero slices, rotation/translation/affine) are used.

"Render all supported volume modes" is compared with pinned napari on frozen reference source, data, hardware, renderer and cache conditions, with numeric/render tolerances and a no-worse rule frozen before the final run; every attempt is kept.

Each applicable injected failure during "Render all supported volume modes" (malformed input, dependency conflict, denied access, missing artifact, low disk, interrupted write, hang/crash, cancel, reconnect, stale revision, failed upgrade, revoked authorization, incomplete cleanup) is reported, leaves unrelated jobs, acquisition, saved work and generations intact, terminates owned workers and grants, and a corrected retry succeeds; the first failure evidence is kept.
"Render all supported volume modes" begins through ordinary Open, Project Data, layer controls, Tools or a declared panel of the installed app, with no private fixture injection.

"Render all supported volume modes" is operated with representative mouse/trackpad and keyboard paths; focus, labels and help, disabled reasons, shortcut conflicts and the current selection are correct.
Switching Tab or Project, closing and reopening the panel or window and restarting the app during "Render all supported volume modes" keep background work on its original input and destination.

After "Render all supported volume modes", the exact saved scientific values, features, relations and provenance are inspected, then exported and reimported (or reopened across OSes where applicable).
"Render all supported volume modes" repeats at the declared viewport sizes and device-pixel scales, resizing during interaction, with no clipping and an exact screen-to-data mapping.
"Render all supported volume modes" shows preview versus accepted state, busy, error and cancel states, and stale/conflict recovery, preserving drafts and other unsaved layers.

children.criteria: Every mapped parametrized case executes in the production-path browser and passes with zero skips; states are equal after normalization (floats to 12 significant digits, frozen before the first comparison run).
children.hooke_equivalent: The Studio's View controls of a scientific session (Data, Open result, Open session; the View tab; Apply view changes), over the confined napari review worker.
children.oracle: The pinned reference. After each recipe, the session's napari state equals the state plain pinned napari reaches by applying the requirement's own setter with the same values: each layer's public state, its data by digest, and the camera. Examples are rendering, attenuation, iso_threshold, interpolation3d, depiction, plane, experimental_clipping_planes, shading, the wireframe and normals parts, and camera.update. The reference rebuilt from the session's layer-data tuples first equals the session. The control also shows the value the worker reports back, and the rendered preview's pixels change. For the isosurface threshold, a higher threshold lights fewer pixels; the Shading control offers exactly none, flat and smooth, and each renders the mesh differently. No matched native screenshot is claimed.
children.procedure: A private Hooke (its own home, assets and empty keys; no camera, keychain or phone; free ports) serves the production Studio build. A fresh browser profile opens a retained 3D volume, and another a retained surface mesh (captured from the same worker as an ordinary output), from Project Data (Data, Open result, Open session, Refresh preview) in the prepared confined napari review bundle (`NAPARI_NATIVE_HOST_PREPARATION`). It operates the ordinary View controls and presses Apply view changes (services/tests/scientific_browser_p2.mjs, `HOOKE_BROWSER`). Before each Apply it records the control's upstream equivalent, and after each recipe it reads the session's napari state through Studio's own Python console. A plain pinned-napari process (`NAPARI_REFERENCE_PYTHON -I`, services/tests/scientific_reference_replay.py) rebuilds the same layers from their layer-data tuples and replays the equivalents. Run by tests/test_scientific_browser_p2.py in `make scientific-acceptance`.

"Use Image layers" is compared with pinned napari on frozen reference source, data, hardware, renderer and cache conditions, with numeric/render tolerances and a no-worse rule frozen before the final run; every attempt is kept.

Each applicable injected failure during "Use Image layers" (malformed input, dependency conflict, denied access, missing artifact, low disk, interrupted write, hang/crash, cancel, reconnect, stale revision, failed upgrade, revoked authorization, incomplete cleanup) is reported, leaves unrelated jobs, acquisition, saved work and generations intact, terminates owned workers and grants, and a corrected retry succeeds; the first failure evidence is kept.
"Use Image layers" begins through ordinary Open, Project Data, layer controls, Tools or a declared panel of the installed app, with no private fixture injection.
"Use Image layers" is operated with representative mouse/trackpad and keyboard paths; focus, labels and help, disabled reasons, shortcut conflicts and the current selection are correct.
Switching Tab or Project, closing and reopening the panel or window and restarting the app during "Use Image layers" keep background work on its original input and destination.
After "Use Image layers", the exact saved scientific values, features, relations and provenance are inspected, then exported and reimported (or reopened across OSes where applicable).
"Use Image layers" repeats at the declared viewport sizes and device-pixel scales, resizing during interaction, with no clipping and an exact screen-to-data mapping.
"Use Image layers" shows preview versus accepted state, busy, error and cancel states, and stale/conflict recovery, preserving drafts and other unsaved layers.

A mixed seven-layer scene (points with features/text, varied shapes, surface topology/values, vectors, division-containing tracks, Image/Labels with matching transforms) keeps stable identity through edits, reordering and export.

"Use Points layers" is compared with pinned napari on frozen reference source, data, hardware, renderer and cache conditions, with numeric/render tolerances and a no-worse rule frozen before the final run; every attempt is kept.

Each applicable injected failure during "Use Points layers" (malformed input, dependency conflict, denied access, missing artifact, low disk, interrupted write, hang/crash, cancel, reconnect, stale revision, failed upgrade, revoked authorization, incomplete cleanup) is reported, leaves unrelated jobs, acquisition, saved work and generations intact, terminates owned workers and grants, and a corrected retry succeeds; the first failure evidence is kept.
"Use Points layers" begins through ordinary Open, Project Data, layer controls, Tools or a declared panel of the installed app, with no private fixture injection.
"Use Points layers" is operated with representative mouse/trackpad and keyboard paths; focus, labels and help, disabled reasons, shortcut conflicts and the current selection are correct.
Switching Tab or Project, closing and reopening the panel or window and restarting the app during "Use Points layers" keep background work on its original input and destination.
After "Use Points layers", the exact saved scientific values, features, relations and provenance are inspected, then exported and reimported (or reopened across OSes where applicable).
"Use Points layers" repeats at the declared viewport sizes and device-pixel scales, resizing during interaction, with no clipping and an exact screen-to-data mapping.
"Use Points layers" shows preview versus accepted state, busy, error and cancel states, and stale/conflict recovery, preserving drafts and other unsaved layers.

"Control connected fill and label preservation" is compared with pinned napari on frozen reference source, data, hardware, renderer and cache conditions, with numeric/render tolerances and a no-worse rule frozen before the final run; every attempt is kept.

Each applicable injected failure during "Control connected fill and label preservation" (malformed input, dependency conflict, denied access, missing artifact, low disk, interrupted write, hang/crash, cancel, reconnect, stale revision, failed upgrade, revoked authorization, incomplete cleanup) is reported, leaves unrelated jobs, acquisition, saved work and generations intact, terminates owned workers and grants, and a corrected retry succeeds; the first failure evidence is kept.
"Control connected fill and label preservation" begins through ordinary Open, Project Data, layer controls, Tools or a declared panel of the installed app, with no private fixture injection.

"Control connected fill and label preservation" is operated with representative mouse/trackpad and keyboard paths; focus, labels and help, disabled reasons, shortcut conflicts and the current selection are correct.

Switching Tab or Project, closing and reopening the panel or window and restarting the app during "Control connected fill and label preservation" keep background work on its original input and destination.

After "Control connected fill and label preservation", the exact saved scientific values, features, relations and provenance are inspected, then exported and reimported (or reopened across OSes where applicable).
"Control connected fill and label preservation" repeats at the declared viewport sizes and device-pixel scales, resizing during interaction, with no clipping and an exact screen-to-data mapping.
"Control connected fill and label preservation" shows preview versus accepted state, busy, error and cancel states, and stale/conflict recovery, preserving drafts and other unsaved layers.

children.hooke_equivalent: Preview keyboard (napari's default Labels bindings) and the Edit section's Labels fields
children.oracle: Three ways: the actual review worker's native result (one shared P4 snapshot read through the Python panel: every changed voxel with its old and new value, the layer's tool state and history) and what the Studio shows must equal the same edit in a plain pinned napari Viewer process on the prepared runtime's own Python, driven through napari's own mouse callbacks and actions at the world positions napari's canvas_to_world gives for the frame pixels the Studio sent (tests/scientific_annotation_reference.py), and the independent numpy expectations of the fixture's definition (tests/scientific_annotation_fixture.py). Executed by tests/test_scientific_annotation_browser.py::test_napari_labels_shortcuts_on_the_preview_run_napari_s_own_actions, and by the harness self-check test_the_comparison_catches_a_worker_whose_napari_editing_was_broken, which breaks napari's Labels.paint and Points.add inside the worker and needs the same comparisons to fail.
children.procedure: Isolated profile: a new Chromium profile (HOOKE_BROWSER) on a private orchestrator with an empty home, no camera and the Studio rebuilt from the checkout (its build identity must equal the backend). The P4 fixture (a 3x4x36x44 uint64 Labels array, t/z/y/x, calibrated 2/1.5/0.5/0.25 with translate 10/-3/5/7, holding a box of label 5, an object of label 2**60+3 with a hole and two disconnected blobs of label 9 on the plane t=1, z=2, and other objects on other planes) is a saved scene document of the prepared annotation review integration (NAPARI_ANNOTATION_PREPARATION), opened from Project Data (Open result, then Open session).  Then: Click the preview with the Inspect tool to focus it, then press napari's default Labels keys 1-6, E, P, F, L, Z, M, =, =, -, X, X, ], ], [, B, B, B, reading the native tool state and the fields after each.

"Add and edit points" is compared with pinned napari on frozen reference source, data, hardware, renderer and cache conditions, with numeric/render tolerances and a no-worse rule frozen before the final run; every attempt is kept.

Each applicable injected failure during "Add and edit points" (malformed input, dependency conflict, denied access, missing artifact, low disk, interrupted write, hang/crash, cancel, reconnect, stale revision, failed upgrade, revoked authorization, incomplete cleanup) is reported, leaves unrelated jobs, acquisition, saved work and generations intact, terminates owned workers and grants, and a corrected retry succeeds; the first failure evidence is kept.
"Add and edit points" begins through ordinary Open, Project Data, layer controls, Tools or a declared panel of the installed app, with no private fixture injection.
"Add and edit points" is operated with representative mouse/trackpad and keyboard paths; focus, labels and help, disabled reasons, shortcut conflicts and the current selection are correct.
Switching Tab or Project, closing and reopening the panel or window and restarting the app during "Add and edit points" keep background work on its original input and destination.
After "Add and edit points", the exact saved scientific values, features, relations and provenance are inspected, then exported and reimported (or reopened across OSes where applicable).
"Add and edit points" repeats at the declared viewport sizes and device-pixel scales, resizing during interaction, with no clipping and an exact screen-to-data mapping.
"Add and edit points" shows preview versus accepted state, busy, error and cancel states, and stale/conflict recovery, preserving drafts and other unsaved layers.

Then in the Studio's Python panel run recipe shape-create.activate-add-line-mode of tests/scientific_annotation_api.py: it makes its own Points or Shapes layer beside the session's layers, does one call, napari mouse callback or napari action, and prints its result.
children.requirement: Offer the action "Add lines" (`activate_add_line_mode`) with its pinned-upstream effect.
upstream_limits: Reference editing is limited to two displayed dimensions.

children.oracle: Three ways: the worker's native layer after the Studio's input (the shared P4 snapshot through the Python panel) must equal plain pinned napari after replaying exactly the annotate requests the Studio sent (read from the browser's network log): napari's own actions, and the pointer and Shift events as real vispy events on napari's own canvas at the same canvas size and camera, paced past napari's 5 ms mouse-move throttle (tests/scientific_annotation_reference.py replay). And the procedure's independent expectation, computed from the pointer positions sent through the camera formula (tests/test_scientific_annotation_browser.py). Every key pressed must also be one of napari's own default bindings for the action it ran. Executed by tests/test_scientific_annotation_browser.py::test_shapes_are_created_on_the_preview_exactly_as_napari_creates_them[delete-during-creation], and by the harness self-check test_the_comparison_catches_a_worker_whose_napari_editing_was_broken.

The 'bermuda' requires the optional 'bermuda' package.
The 'partsegcore' requires the optional 'partsegcore-compiled-backend' package.
The 'triangle' requires the optional 'triangle' package.
The 'numba' backend requires the optional 'numba' package.
The 'pure python' backend uses the default Python triangulation from vispy.
The 'fastest available' backend will select the fastest available backend.
", validation_alias=AliasChoices('triangulation_backend', 'napari_triangulation_backend'))

children.hooke_equivalent: The session's Python panel (napari's API on the session's viewer)
children.oracle: Three ways: the recipe's result in the actual review worker (run through the Studio's Python panel, printed as JSON) must equal the same recipe in a plain pinned napari Viewer process on the prepared runtime's own Python holding the same session layers (tests/scientific_annotation_reference.py), and the result its definition requires, written independently in tests/scientific_annotation_api.py. Executed by tests/test_scientific_annotation_browser.py::test_points_and_shapes_editing_api_in_the_worker_is_napari_s[shape-create.setting-experimentalsettings-triangulation-backend], and by the harness self-check test_the_comparison_catches_a_worker_whose_napari_editing_was_broken.
children.procedure: Isolated profile: a new Chromium profile (HOOKE_BROWSER) on a private orchestrator with an empty home, no camera and the Studio rebuilt from the checkout (its build identity must equal the backend). The P4 fixture (a 3x4x36x44 uint64 Labels array, t/z/y/x, calibrated 2/1.5/0.5/0.25 with translate 10/-3/5/7, holding a box of label 5, an object of label 2**60+3 with a hole and two disconnected blobs of label 9 on the plane t=1, z=2, and other objects on other planes) is a saved scene document of the prepared annotation review integration (NAPARI_ANNOTATION_PREPARATION), opened from Project Data (Open result, then Open session). Then in the Studio's Python panel run recipe shape-create.setting-experimentalsettings-triangulation-backend of tests/scientific_annotation_api.py: it makes its own Points or Shapes layer beside the session's layers, does one call, napari mouse callback or napari action, and prints its result.
children.requirement: Honour the setting `ExperimentalSettings.triangulation_backend` with its pinned-upstream default and effect.
upstream_limits: Reference editing is limited to two displayed dimensions.

children.oracle: Three ways: the worker's native layer after the Studio's input (the shared P4 snapshot through the Python panel) must equal plain pinned napari after replaying exactly the annotate requests the Studio sent (read from the browser's network log): napari's own actions, and the pointer and Shift events as real vispy events on napari's own canvas at the same canvas size and camera, paced past napari's 5 ms mouse-move throttle (tests/scientific_annotation_reference.py replay). children.oracle: Three ways: the worker's native layer after the Studio's input (the shared P4 snapshot through the Python panel) must equal plain pinned napari after replaying exactly the annotate requests the Studio sent (read from the browser's network log): napari's own actions, and the pointer and Shift events as real vispy events on napari's own canvas at the same canvas size and camera, paced past napari's 5 ms mouse-move throttle (tests/scientific_annotation_reference.py replay). And the procedure's independent expectation, computed from the pointer positions sent through the camera formula (tests/test_scientific_annotation_browser.py). Every key pressed must also be one of napari's own default bindings for the action it ran. Executed by tests/test_scientific_annotation_browser.py::test_shapes_are_edited_on_the_preview_exactly_as_napari_edits_them[upstream-limit-ellipse-direct-unsupported], and by the harness self-check test_the_comparison_catches_a_worker_whose_napari_editing_was_broken.
children.procedure: Isolated profile: a new Chromium profile (HOOKE_BROWSER) on a private orchestrator with an empty home, no camera and the Studio rebuilt from the checkout (its build identity must equal the backend). The P4 fixture (a 3x4x36x44 uint64 Labels array, t/z/y/x, calibrated 2/1.5/0.5/0.25 with translate 10/-3/5/7, holding a box of label 5, an object of label 2**60+3 with a hole and two disconnected blobs of label 9 on the plane t=1, z=2, and other objects on other planes) is a saved scene document of the prepared annotation review integration (NAPARI_ANNOTATION_PREPARATION), opened from Project Data (Open result, then Open session). The annotated Points or Shapes layer is created in the session's Python panel (setup) with napari's own test coordinates (data 0-100 at scale 0.1, translate 5/7, inside the view): for Shapes the fixture F, a rectangle (20,30)-(40,60) and a triangle (60,20),(60,50),(80,35), or the procedure's own shapes.  Then: In the Edit section's annotation panel choose the layer and its napari mode, then operate procedure upstream-limit-ellipse-direct-unsupported of tests/test_scientific_annotation_browser.py EDIT: real pointer presses, drags, clicks and double clicks on the preview, Shift held where the procedure says, and napari's keys on the focused preview or the panel's buttons.

A multi-actor lifecycle (two views, two kernels, concurrent manual/plugin updates, Projects/Tabs switched during work, inactive/closed windows, delayed replies, differing bundle generations).

"Run viewer callbacks safely" is compared with pinned napari on frozen reference source, data, hardware, renderer and cache conditions, with numeric/render tolerances and a no-worse rule frozen before the final run; every attempt is kept.

Each applicable injected failure during "Run viewer callbacks safely" (malformed input, dependency conflict, denied access, missing artifact, low disk, interrupted write, hang/crash, cancel, reconnect, stale revision, failed upgrade, revoked authorization, incomplete cleanup) is reported, leaves unrelated jobs, acquisition, saved work and generations intact, terminates owned workers and grants, and a corrected retry succeeds; the first failure evidence is kept.
"Run viewer callbacks safely" begins through ordinary Open, Project Data, layer controls, Tools or a declared panel of the installed app, with no private fixture injection.
"Run viewer callbacks safely" is operated with representative mouse/trackpad and keyboard paths; focus, labels and help, disabled reasons, shortcut conflicts and the current selection are correct.
Switching Tab or Project, closing and reopening the panel or window and restarting the app during "Run viewer callbacks safely" keep background work on its original input and destination.
After "Run viewer callbacks safely", the exact saved scientific values, features, relations and provenance are inspected, then exported and reimported (or reopened across OSes where applicable).
"Run viewer callbacks safely" repeats at the declared viewport sizes and device-pixel scales, resizing during interaction, with no clipping and an exact screen-to-data mapping.
"Run viewer callbacks safely" shows preview versus accepted state, busy, error and cancel states, and stale/conflict recovery, preserving drafts and other unsaved layers.
